dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:6601.text: Being 𡰉𡯗, awkward or impeded. Formed from 尣, with 介 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6602.text: Walking with the shins crossing. Formed from 尣, with 勺 indicating the sound. A cow crossing its legs as it walks is called 尦.

shuowen:6603.text: When someone lame cannot walk and is led by another, this is called 𡰖𡰡. Formed from 尣 and 爪, with 是 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6604.text: Being 𡰖𡰡, led along while unable to walk. Formed from 尣 and 爪, with 巂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6605.text: A bent or impaired thigh. Formed from 尣, with 于 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6606.text: An ailment in the knee. Formed from 尣 and 羸.

shuowen:6607.text: A round vessel of Kunwu. A pictograph. Includes 大, representing its lid. All characters in the 壷 group are formed from 壷.

shuowen:6608.text: The mingling expressed by 壹㚃. Formed from 凶 and 壺: being unable to escape is 凶. The Changes says: 'Heaven and earth mingle as one.'

shuowen:6609.text: Single and undivided. Formed from 壺, with 吉 indicating the sound. All characters in the 壹 group are formed from 壹.

shuowen:6610.text: Single-minded, enduring, and fine. Formed from 壹, with an abbreviated 恣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6611.text: Something used to startle people. Formed from 大 and 𢆉. Another explanation: a loud sound. All characters in this group are formed from 㚔. Another reading is like 瓠. Another explanation: in popular speech, persistent thieving is called 㚔, read like 籋.

shuowen:6612.text: To watch with the eyes. Formed from a horizontal 目 and 㚔: ordering officials to watch for and arrest offenders.

shuowen:6613.text: To arrest an offender. Formed from 丮 and 㚔; 㚔 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:6614.text: A prison, used to detain offenders. Formed from 㚔 and 囗. Another explanation: a boundary. Another: 圉人 are those responsible for horses.

shuowen:6615.text: To pull and strike. Formed from 㚔 and 攴, with blood visible. There is a Zhouzhi county in Fufeng.

shuowen:6616.text: To adjudge an offender's punishment. Formed from 㚔 and 𠬝. 𠬝 means to submit to punishment.

shuowen:6617.text: To investigate an offender exhaustively. Formed from 㚔, 人, and 言, with 竹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6618.text: To spread out. Formed from 大, with 者 indicating the sound. All characters in the 奢 group are formed from 奢.

shuowen:6619.text: The appearance of abundant wealth. Formed from 奢, with 單 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6620.text: A person's neck. Formed from an abbreviated 大, depicting the neck's vessels. All characters in the 亢 group are formed from 亢.

shuowen:6621.text: The appearance of holding the neck stiffly upright and arrogantly. Formed from 亢 and 夋. 夋 means haughty. 亢 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:6622.text: To advance quickly. Formed from 大 and 十: 大十 is like combining ten people. All characters in the 𠦍 group are formed from 𠦍. Read like 滔.

shuowen:6623.text: Swift. Formed from 𠦍, with 卉 indicating the sound. 拜 is formed from this.

shuowen:6624.text: To hurry toward something. Formed from 日, 出, and 𠦍, with 廾 supporting it.

shuowen:6625.text: To advance. Formed from 𠦍 and 屮, with 允 indicating the sound. The Changes says: 'Advancing upward brings great good fortune.'

shuowen:6626.text: To present or advance. Formed from 𠦍, 廾, and 屮. 屮 conveys advancing upward.

shuowen:6627.text: The advance of white vapor. Formed from 𠦍 and 白. In ritual, the invoker says 臯; ascending to sing is called 奏. Thus both 臯 and 奏 are formed from 夲. The Rites of Zhou says: 'Call them to come, drum, and perform the 皐 dance.' 皐 means to announce to them.

shuowen:6628.text: To release. Formed from 大 divided by 八. All characters in the 夰 group are formed from 夰.

shuowen:6629.text: Raising the eyes in a startled manner. Formed from 夰 and 䀠; 䀠 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:6630.text: Arrogant. Formed from 𦣻 and 夰; 夰 also indicates the sound. The Book of Yu says: 'Like Danzhu's arrogance.' Read like 傲. The Analects says: 'Ao pushed boats over land.'

shuowen:6631.text: In spring, heaven is called 昦天; the primal vapor is expansive. Formed from 日 and 夰; 夰 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:6632.text: To run in alarm. Another explanation: to come and go. Formed from 夰 and 臦. The Book of Zhou says: 'Bo Guang.' The ancient-script 臦 is an ancient form of 囧.

shuowen:6633.text: The large-seal form 亣 modifies the ancient form. It too depicts a person. All characters in the 亣 group are formed from 亣.

shuowen:6634.text: Great. Formed from 亣, with 亦 indicating the sound. The Odes says: 'Lofty is Mount Liang.'

shuowen:6635.text: Stout and large. Formed from 亣 and 壯; 壯 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:6636.text: Great whiteness; luster. Formed from 亣 and 白. Ancient script uses it as the character 澤.

shuowen:6637.text: A large belly. Formed from 亣, with an abbreviated 𦃟 indicating the sound. 𦃟 is the large-seal form of 系.

shuowen:6638.text: Somewhat larger toward the front. Formed from 亣, with 而 indicating the sound. Read like 偄 in 畏偄.

shuowen:6639.text: A large appearance. Formed from 亣, with 𥆞 indicating the sound. Some say it is the character for valor with the fists. Another reading is like 傿.

shuowen:6640.text: Robust and large. Formed from three 大 and three 目. Two eyes make 𥆞; three make 𡚤, indicating still greater size. Another explanation: to press. Read like 虙 in the Changes' 虙羲氏. The Odes says: 'Anger without drunkenness is called 𡚤.'

shuowen:6641.text: An adult man. Formed from 大, with 一 depicting a hairpin. Under Zhou measures, eight cun make a chi and ten chi make a zhang. A person is eight chi tall, hence the term 丈夫. All characters in this group are formed from 夫.

shuowen:6642.text: To have rules and standards. Formed from 夫 and 見.

shuowen:6643.text: To walk side by side. Formed from two 夫. 輦 is formed from this. Read like 伴 in 伴侶, 'companion.'

shuowen:6644.text: To stand or stay. Formed from 大 standing above 一. All characters in the 立 group are formed from 立.

shuowen:6645.text: To approach or face. Formed from 立 and 隶.

shuowen:6646.text: 磊䇏 means piled up in layers. Formed from 立, with 𦎫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6647.text: Upright. Formed from 立, with 耑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6648.text: To equalize. Formed from 立, with 專 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Discourses of the States says: 'Equalize the root and establish the end.'

shuowen:6649.text: Reverent. Formed from 立 and 束. 束 means to constrain and discipline oneself.

shuowen:6650.text: Quietly settled. Formed from 立, with 爭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6651.text: To stand quietly. Formed from 立, with 青 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a delicate appearance.

shuowen:6652.text: To wait. Formed from 立, with 矣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6653.text: Strong or capable. Another explanation: a craftsman. Formed from 立, with 句 indicating the sound. Read like 齲. The Lost Book of Zhou has the expression 竘匠.

shuowen:6654.text: Not upright. Formed from 立, with 𩰬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6655.text: To bear and lift. Formed from 立, with 曷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6656.text: To wait. Formed from 立, with 須 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6657.text: Weak or withered. Formed from 立, with 𣎆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6658.text: Being 偓竣, waiting respectfully. Formed from 立, with 夋 indicating the sound. The Discourses of the States says: 'The officials, their duties finished, stood waiting.'

shuowen:6659.text: The appearance of seeing a ghost or spirit. Formed from 立 and 录. 录 is the large-seal form of 鬽. Read like 虙 in 虙羲氏.

shuowen:6660.text: A startled appearance. Formed from 立, with 昔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6661.text: The appearance of a short person standing. Formed from 立, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6662.text: A high tower without a roof in the northern regions. Formed from 立, with 曾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6663.text: Together or side by side. Formed from two 立. All characters in the 竝 group are formed from 竝.

shuowen:6664.text: Collapsed, with one side lower. Formed from 竝, with 白 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6665.text: The joining of the skull; the brain's covering. A pictograph. All characters in the 囟 group are formed from 囟.

shuowen:6666.text: Bristling hair. It depicts hair on the 囟 and the shaggy appearance of hair. This is the same as the large-seal character 子.

shuowen:6667.text: A person's navel. Formed from 囟, expressing the passage of vital breath, with 比 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6668.text: To contain or accommodate. Formed from 心, with 囟 indicating the sound. All characters in the 思 group are formed from 思.

shuowen:6669.text: To deliberate and think. Formed from 思, with 虍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6670.text: The human heart, the earth-associated organ, situated in the body's center. A pictograph. The learned doctors explain it as the fire-associated organ. All characters in this group are formed from 心.

shuowen:6671.text: To breathe. Formed from 心 and 自; 自 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:6672.text: The yin vital energy in people that has desires. Formed from 心, with 青 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6673.text: The yang vital energy in people whose nature is good. Formed from 心, with 生 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6674.text: Intention. Formed from 心, with 之 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6675.text: Intention or purpose. One examines speech with the heart and so knows the intention. Formed from 心 and 音.

shuowen:6676.text: Intention. Formed from 心, with 旨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6677.text: To attain outwardly in relation to others and inwardly within oneself. Formed from 直 and 心.

shuowen:6678.text: To correspond. Formed from 心, with 𤸰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6679.text: Careful. Formed from 心, with 眞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6680.text: Reverent. Formed from 心, with 中 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6681.text: Careful. Formed from 心, with 𣪊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6682.text: Fine or beautiful. Formed from 心, with 䫉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6683.text: Joyful. Formed from 心, with 夬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6684.text: Joyful. Formed from 心, with 豈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6685.text: A delighted heart. Formed from 心, with 匧 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6686.text: To think of constantly. Formed from 心, with 今 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6687.text: To think. Formed from 心, with 付 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6688.text: Quick and perceptive. Formed from 心 and 目, with an abbreviated 害 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6689.text: Level or tranquil. Formed from 心, with 登 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6690.text: Reverent. Formed from 心, with 難 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6691.text: To open. Formed from 心, with 斤 indicating the sound. The Methods of the Sima says: 'The good ruler opens the people's goodness and shuts off their wickedness.'

shuowen:6692.text: Slow. Formed from 心, with 重 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6693.text: Grave and substantial. Formed from 心, with 軍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6694.text: Substantial or sincere. Formed from 心, with 𦎫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6695.text: Impassioned, as in 慨. Formed from 心, with 亢 indicating the sound. Another explanation cites the Changes: 'The overreaching dragon has regret.'

shuowen:6696.text: 忼慨 describes a brave man unable to fulfill his aspirations. Formed from 心, with 旣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6697.text: Sincere, as in 愊. Formed from 心, with 困 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6698.text: Sincere intent. Formed from 心, with 畐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6699.text: Careful. Formed from 心, with 原 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6700.text: Clever. Formed from 心, with 彗 indicating the sound.
